newsitem.title: JAPAN: US Treasuries steady, quiet ahead of jobs data.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries steady, quiet ahead of jobs data.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were steady at the Tokyo midday on Friday versus previous New York levels, with many operators taking a wait-and-see stance ahead of U.S. jobs data scheduled for release at 1230 GMT, traders said.
"The market is very slow.... I haven't received many phone calls this morning," a manager at a U.S. brokerage house said.
Traders said the market is speculating that growth in non-farm payrolls in May will be smaller than previously forecast, and this has lent some support to prices recently.
Traders said the data should determine market trends for the longer term.
Economists polled by Reuters estimated on average that 219,000 new jobs were added to non-farm payrolls in May.
"The recent price rises show that the market has already factored in results that would induce strong buying," a Japanese bank trader said.
Traders said prices were steady across the board this morning, with the key 30-year bond unchanged from New York's close at 96-25/32, yielding 6.88 percent.
Traders said that the 10-year Treasury note has been supported recently by vague rumours that the U.S. Treasury may cancel its note auctions in July and October.
"The 10-year note has been performing well on the rumour, but the rumour is very vague," the U.S. brokerage manager said.
The September T-bond futures contact fell 1/32 to 110-1/32 from the previous close.
